doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: The music business, the war and the political climate
summary: Fleck links the bad state of the music business to politics, especially before the election. He is cautious about airing political views and sees national division.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: You do so much traveling. Are there trends that you’ve noticed in the country, either positive or negative, that have made an impression on you?
We’ve seen — the music business is in a bad state right now. And I can’t help but think it’s connected to the political situation.

Well like I don’t like to push my own political views because like now I’m getting to be more well known and stuff and I feel like a lot of people who aren’t as well known don’t get the same forum, so I feel like I like to be cautious about when I speak out. But I mean being at war is tough. Although I do remember there’s been times when the country was at war where the entertainment business was booming. But this time here recently, especially around the election, and the whole six months leading up to the election was some of the worst I’ve seen since — at least since I’ve been in the Flecktones. But now it seems to be picking back up again, now that that decision finally got made, for better or for worse it seems like. Because normally I seem to remember that when times were bad it was often really good for the music business. I mean it doesn’t matter a hill of beans in the big picture of what’s going on in the world, whether the music business is doing good or not. I’m very aware of that. But I can’t help but notice when crowds are off in places that used to be good. But then all of a sudden they’re back. You know I see all those things. I think there’s a lot of confusion and division right now about what the country should do and how we should approach being America. That’s too bad. I mean I wish we could be more together about it.
